properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 2:48PM AKST until November 16 at 1:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 6 and 12 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze
to a few hundredths of an inch.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula, Skilak Lake, and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the interior Kenai
Peninsula by late this evening. Snow will continue through Sunday
evening before warmer air begins to move over the region. Snow will
likely change to rain. However, pockets of freezing rain are
possible in typically colder areas along the Seward Highway from
Turnagain Pass to Primrose.

properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 14 at 12:31PM AKST until November 17 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 45 to 60 mph with gusts up to 75 mph
possible.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...From late Monday night through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adak could see the strongest wind gusts of 75
mph with Atka winds potentially gusting to 60 mph. Winds rapidly
increase in strength late Monday evening and peak late Tuesday
morning as a strong low pressure system moves through the Bering.
Winds will gradually lighten but remain gusty through Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 14 at 12:03PM AKST until November 14 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Along Glenn Highway from downtown Anchorage to Knik River
Bridge.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility. Below
freezing temperatures may lead to frost on bridges and roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of locally dense fog have developed
around Knik Arm and along parts of the Glenn and Parks Highway
overnight. Areas of dense fog beginning to lift across portions of
the area, but some particularly patchy dense fog linger across the
Anchorage Bowl and Mat-Su Valleys. Visibility could quickly change
along the Glenn Highway.
properties.instruction:
A dense fog advisory means visibilities will frequently be reduced to
less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 10:42AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait
and the waters around western Kodiak Island. These winds are
resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption, causing
haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation. The
villages of Karluk and Larsen Bay are most likely to be impacted.

Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are
encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling
the ash. The winds should weaken Saturday night.

NWSheadline: RESUSPENDED ASH FROM KATMAI-NOVARUPTA EXPECTED OVER SOUTHERN KODIAK ISLAND THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
